full.rationale: Rust payload rebaselined 2026-08-08 for 1.8.4: +287,744 bytes over the 1.7.5 reference, which overran the previous 256 KiB allowance by 25,600 bytes. The growth is the 1.8.x work measured against a 1.7.5 baseline, not one release's worth: the QuickLook-parity preview batch and its transport strip, the SQLite database view, the portable registration path, and 1.8.4's own additions - the icon-style format badge (src/badge.rs: a seven-tint category palette and the dog-eared page silhouette), src/checkerpx.rs, src/typeoverlay.rs, and three new doctor checks including the shell round-trip that finally distinguishes 'our decoder works but Explorer drops it' (issue #16). The INSTALLER reference moved with it, to 1.8.4: the compressed setup grew 132,710 bytes over the 1.7.5 reference and overran the 128 KiB allowance by 1,638 bytes, which is the same Rust growth after compression and not a new payload. The magick budget is UNCHANGED and was not what tripped. The 1.7.5 rationale (the from-scratch JPEG 2000 reduced-resolution decoder in src/decode/jp2) still holds and is still in this payload. Keep later releases within 128 KiB compressed and 256 KiB for each raw payload unless an explicit reviewed policy change records why.

ARM64 installer AND Rust payload rebaselined 2026-08-09 for 1.8.5. Same stale-reference shape as the 1.8.0 entry this replaces: the installer reference was still 12,146,914 bytes from 1.8.0-arm64-full-stubbed while x64 was rebaselined at 1.8.4, so the 137,412 bytes measured here are FIVE releases of accumulated, already-reviewed growth (1.8.1 through 1.8.5), not one release's worth. It overran the 128 KiB installer allowance by 6,340 bytes. Evidence that 1.8.5 itself is not the cause: x64, whose reference IS current (1.8.4), grew only 5,150 bytes of installer and 31,232 bytes of payload in this same release and passed with 125,922 bytes of headroom. The growth is the work x64 already absorbed at its 1.8.4 rebaseline - the icon-style format badge (src/badge.rs), src/checkerpx.rs, src/typeoverlay.rs and the doctor shell round-trip - plus 1.8.5's own src/vcodec.rs (video codec identification and the Media Foundation decoder probe). The Rust payload is rebaselined in the SAME edit rather than left alone: it PASSED, but with only 47,104 bytes of headroom (215,040 of its 256 KiB allowance already consumed against that same stale 1.8.0 reference), so leaving it would hand the next release a near-exhausted budget and a failure that has nothing to do with that release either. Magick budget UNCHANGED and was not what tripped. Installer 12284326 bytes, SHA-256 e187e5c2d61cb0745ae67f20f214c69ccb19df26375619058dfdbe9e837f28f0. Keep later releases within 128 KiB compressed and 256 KiB for each raw payload unless an explicit reviewed policy change records why. The stubs are built with the MSVC ARM64 toolchain (cl + link /DEF /IMPLIB) rather than MinGW, because MinGW emits x86_64 PEs regardless of target - the first ARM64 Full build silently replaced genuine ARM64 DLLs with x64 stubs, which an ARM64 loader refuses. gendef still extracts the exports for both architectures, since a PE export table is architecture-independent. link's /IMPLIB is load-bearing: without it the linker drops <name>.lib and <name>.exp beside /OUT, straight into the shipped bundle. harfbuzz and fribidi end up fully pruned once stubbing removes their importers, which is why the file count is 155. Every staged PE is asserted to be machine 0xAA64. NOTE: published 1.6.0 shipped the UNSTUBBED arm64 payload (13,589,408-byte installer); this reference applies from the next release.
